questions.question: Which formula is an example of a function defined on $\mathbb{R}$?
options: $f(x) = \sqrt{x}$ on $(-\infty,0)$
$x = y^2$ with two possible $y$ values
$f(x)$ has no output for any $x$

questions.question: For $f(x) = x^2$ defined on $\mathbb{R}$, what is $f(3)$?
How is the range related to the codomain?
options: The codomain is always a subset of the range.
The range must be empty.
The range is unrelated to outputs.
The range is a subset of the codomain.

questions.question: How many points can any vertical line share with the graph of a real-valued function of one real variable?
options: meets the graph at most once
meets the graph at least twice
is parallel to the graph
passes through the origin

questions.question: Which relation from $X = \{1,2\}$ to $Y = \{a,b\}$ defines a function?
options: $1\mapsto a$ and $2\mapsto b$
$1\mapsto a$, $1\mapsto b$, and $2\mapsto b$
$1\mapsto a$ and no output for $2$
No input in $X$ has an output

questions.question: For $f(x) = \sqrt{x}$ defined on $[0,+\infty)$, which input is allowed by the stated domain?
Which failure prevents a proposed rule from being a function $X\to Y$?
options: The outputs lie in $Y$ but not in the domain $X$.
Each $x\in X$ is paired with the same output $y\in Y$.
Some $x\in X$ has two different assigned outputs in $Y$.
The inverse rule from $Y$ back to $X$ is not a function.

questions.question: Why does the definition mention both domain and codomain?
options: They are optional labels; the formula alone fixes $f$
They specify allowed inputs and the output set
They list exactly the inputs used and the outputs hit
They ensure every output comes from exactly one input

questions.question: A rule on $X = \{1,2,3\}$ assigns outputs only to $1$ and $2$. Is it a function on $X$?
options: Yes, because no input in $X$ is given two outputs.
Yes, if we shrink the codomain to the outputs used.
No, because functions cannot have finite domains.
No, because every $x\in X$ must have exactly one output.

questions.question: Why is $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ on $[0,\infty)$ a function, even though $4$ has square roots $\pm2$?
options: It uses the principal root
It assigns both $+2$ and $-2$ to $4$
It is not actually a function
It only works for perfect squares

questions.question: Can two different inputs of a function have the same output?
options: Yes; shared outputs are allowed
No; all outputs must be distinct
No; that makes it fail to be a function
Only if the function is constant

questions.question: When are two functions regarded as equal?
options: When all three defining parts agree
When they share at least one output value
When their formulas merely look similar
When they have the same range only

questions.question: Which rule from $\{1,2\}$ to $\{a,b\}$ is not a function?
options: $1\mapsto a$ and $1\mapsto b$ with $2\mapsto a$.
$1\mapsto a$ and $2\mapsto a$, so $b$ is never used.
$1\mapsto b$ and $2\mapsto b$, so both share $b$.
$2\mapsto a$ and $1\mapsto b$, listed with $2$ first.

questions.question: For $f(x)=x^2$ with domain $\{-1,0,1\}$, what is the range?
Which of these is a valid function from $\mathbb{R}$ to $\mathbb{R}$?
options: $f(x)=3$ for every $x$
a rule giving two outputs when $x=1$
a rule with no output for $x=0$
the relation $x=y^2$

questions.question: Why can the codomain be larger than the range?
options: The range counts each output once, the codomain with repeats
The codomain must also contain every element of $X$
Some inputs may lack outputs, shrinking the range
The codomain is allowed outputs; the range is hit

questions.question: Let $X=\{1,2\}$, $Y=\{a,b,c\}$, and define $f(1)=a$, $f(2)=a$. What is the range?
options: $\varnothing$
